note.p: On 5 August 1816, Godwin travels to Aylesbury. He notes 'Drake's Agmondesham - the latter being the name of a rotten borough in what is now Buckinghamshire which returned two members of Parliament until the Reform Act of 1832. Godwin may have referred to it as Drake's Agmondesham because the borough systematically returned members of the Drake family - at the time Godwin was there it would probably have been William Drake senr and William Drake junr. It is possible, but unlikely that Godwin made their acquaintance. The next day's entry shows that Godwin calls on Mackintosh, who lived near Aylesbury - and was the main object of his visit. He notes that he sleeps - possibly at Mackintosh's house- but also mentions the jail at Aylesbury, which he probably visited.
